comment: The suite. run.sh sets each scene; this file states what the action must decide. 'reason' is a regex the logged reason must match; for an approval or a merge, 'review' is a regex its body must match too; 'event', when set, is the only event whose runs count. Regexes are ERE, matched by Bash. 'inputs' and 'rules' are what each scenario proves; scripts/pr-approval/e2e.test.js fails when an action.yml input or a rule has neither a scenario nor an exemption here (E2E-001).

scenarios.name: custom-approved
scenarios.summary: A harness PR into develop that meets the custom policy is approved.

scenarios.name: no-policy
scenarios.summary: A PR into main that is not a promotion matches no policy.

scenarios.name: outside-paths
scenarios.summary: A file outside the policy's paths refuses the PR.
scenarios.reason: ^\[e2e-change: APPROVE-002\] changes outside\.txt, outside the allowed paths$

scenarios.name: policy-from-base
scenarios.summary: A head that widens the policy to allow itself is still judged by the base's policy.
scenarios.reason: ^\[e2e-change: APPROVE-002\] changes \.strspc/pr-approval\.yml, outside the allowed paths$

scenarios.name: ci-failing
scenarios.summary: A failed check refuses the PR.

scenarios.name: dry-run
scenarios.summary: With dry-run on, the action reports what it would do and writes nothing.
scenarios.reason: ^\[e2e-change: APPROVE-002\] would approve: custom \(policy conditions met\)$

scenarios.name: ci-fail-withdraws
scenarios.summary: A check that fails after the approval, on the same head, withdraws it.

scenarios.name: promotion-approved
scenarios.summary: A promotion whose every commit came from an approved PR is approved, and not merged: its policy leaves merging off although the merge token is set.
scenarios.reason: ^\[promotion: APPROVE-005\] (already approved: )?promotion \(develop to main, 1 commit\(s\) from 1 approved PR\(s\)\)$
scenarios.review: ^Approved under policy `promotion` \(APPROVE-005\): promotion \(develop to main, 1 commit\(s\) from 1 approved PR\(s\)\)

scenarios.name: promotion-unapproved
scenarios.summary: A promotion carrying a commit from a PR merged without approval is refused (the 0w3 case).
scenarios.reason: ^\[promotion: APPROVE-005\] commit [0-9a-f]{8} came from #[0-9]+, which has no standing approval$

scenarios.name: release-merged
scenarios.summary: A release-please PR is approved, then merged by the testbed App with a merge commit, and the merge starts a workflow on main.

scenarios.name: sweep-approves
scenarios.summary: A PR its own events left unapproved is approved by a dispatch of the caller.

exemptions.policy-token: The sandbox's policy extends nothing, so no remote policy file is fetched; resolving extends: with this token is covered by policy.test.js.
exemptions.allow-no-checks: Every sandbox PR has the CI stub's check, so the no-checks path never arises there; decide.test.js covers it both ways.
exemptions.companion-workflow: The sandbox runs no strspc-pr-review caller, so there is no companion run to ignore; decide.test.js covers the exemption.

rule_exemptions.APPROVE-001: Forks, drafts and self-authored PRs are stopped by the caller's job if: or by the first guard; decide.test.js covers each, and a fork PR cannot be opened by the harness's single account.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-003: A change between the reads needs an edit timed inside one run; decide.test.js drives it with a fake API.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-004: The sandbox rulesets dismiss an approval on every push, so GitHub withdraws it before the action could; decide.test.js covers head and base changes.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-007: No sync-back scenario yet: it needs a release branch and release-please's files on both sides. kinds/sync-back.test.js covers it.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-008: No rules-pin scenario yet: the pin PRs come from steerspec-sync. kinds/pin.test.js covers it.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-009: No template-sync scenario yet: those PRs come from steerspec-sync with its label. kinds/template-sync.test.js covers it.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-010: A property of every kind's validation, not of one run; policy.test.js and decide.test.js try to relax the built-in conditions.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-011: The evaluator veto is not built yet (v1.1); there is nothing to run.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-012: Needs another account's approval for the action to leave alone; decide.test.js covers that only marked approvals of its own are withdrawn.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-013: The sandbox has no Copilot review; copilot.test.js and decide.test.js cover the veto.
rule_exemptions.APPROVE-015: Needs a check to fail between the approval and the re-read inside one run; decide.test.js drives that interleaving.
rule_exemptions.POLICY-002: The sandbox's policy extends nothing; policy.test.js refuses branch refs.
rule_exemptions.POLICY-003: The sandbox's policy extends nothing; policy.test.js covers cycles and depth.
rule_exemptions.POLICY-004: An invalid policy on the sandbox's base would break every other scenario run after it; policy.test.js covers the schema.
rule_exemptions.POLICY-005: Checked when the policy loads, before any PR; policy.test.js covers it, and the sandbox's own policy cites a rule in each entry.
rule_exemptions.POLICY-006: No two sandbox policies match the same PR; policy.test.js covers first-match order.
rule_exemptions.MERGE-003: release-merged shows the clean path; a refusal needs the head to move or the state to change inside one run, which merge.test.js drives.
rule_exemptions.MERGE-005: Needs a release PR while develop holds an unpromoted changelog-visible commit; kinds/release.test.js and merge.test.js cover it.
